messages.subject: Multivariate growth with time-invariant variable
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am analyzing the covariance of intercepts and slopes of two constructs in a multivariate growth curve model and I want to look for group differences in this covariance. Unfortunately, I couldn´t find any lavaan example on this. I know how to analyse group differences by  i + s ~ group, but this shows differences in slope and intercept, not group differences in the covariance of two constructs in a multivariate model?

The only thing I can do is including group by "group=..." into the model fit, but by this I can´t see significant differences between groups.

I am grateful for any advice!

My analysis are based on the following example --> step 4 in lavaan, but without time-varying covariate: https://quantdev.ssri.psu.edu/tutorials/growth-modeling-chapter-8-multivariate-growth-models-and-dynamic-parameters

Many thanks in advance!

Best regards,
Deni

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multivariate growth with time-invariant variable
parts:
In a multigroup model, you can provide a vector of parameter labels (or same label to impose an equality constraint):

https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html

But covariances are not necessarily comparable if the variances are not the same across groups.  If you want to compare correlations, you can create a "phantom construct" for each growth factor:

ph_i =~ c(NA, NA)*i
i ~~ c(0, 0)*i
ph_i ~~ c(1, 1)*ph_i + c(0, 0)*s

ph_s =~ c(NA, NA)*s
s ~~ c(0, 0)*s
ph_s ~~ c(1, 1)*ph_s + c(0, 0)*i

i ~~ c(0, 0)*s

ph_i ~~ c(cor1, cor2)*ph_s

cor_diff := cor1 - cor2

The last line is a user-defined parameter: the group difference in correlations.  So you can get a Wald z test from the summary() to test whether they are equal.  Or use a LRT by fitting a nested model with the same label for both groups: ph_i ~~ c(cor1, cor1)*ph_s

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

In model2 with the difference calculation, the value for group 1 is the same, but negative: -.45
